questions.stem: The functional unit of the human kidney is called the:

options.option_text: Nephron — each kidney has approximately 1 million nephrons filtering blood
Glomerulus — the glomerulus is a component of the nephron, not the whole unit
Ureter — the ureter is the tube carrying urine from kidney to bladder
Loop of Henle — this is one structural part of the nephron, not the entire unit

questions.explanation: NEPHRON: structural and functional unit of the kidney. COMPONENTS: Bowman's capsule + glomerulus (filtration), PCT, Loop of Henle, DCT, collecting duct. URINE FORMATION: Filtration (glomerulus) → Reabsorption (PCT, loop, DCT) → Secretion (DCT) → Concentration (collecting duct). COUNT: ~1 million nephrons per kidney. CORTICAL NEPHRONS: short loop; JUXTAMEDULLARY NEPHRONS: long loop, concentrate urine better. PYQ: nephron = functional unit — SSC CGL, IBPS PO, UPSC standard 1-marker.

questions.stem: The process by which blood is filtered under pressure in the kidney to produce a cell-free, protein-free filtrate is called:

options.option_text: Ultrafiltration (glomerular filtration) — high hydrostatic pressure forces plasma through capillary walls
Tubular reabsorption — this takes useful substances BACK into blood from the filtrate
Tubular secretion — this adds additional waste FROM blood INTO the tubule lumen instead
Osmosis — osmosis is passive water movement; kidney filtration is pressure-driven

questions.explanation: ULTRAFILTRATION: blood enters glomerulus under high pressure. Water, urea, glucose, ions, amino acids → filtered into Bowman's capsule. RETAINED: RBCs, WBCs, large proteins. GFR: ~125 mL/min; ~180 L/day filtered; only ~1.5 L/day excreted. TUBULAR REABSORPTION: PCT reabsorbs ~65-70% of water, all glucose and amino acids. ADH: increases water reabsorption in collecting duct → concentrated urine. PYQ: ultrafiltration vs reabsorption in UPSC, IBPS PO.

questions.stem: Humans are classified as ureotelic organisms because our primary nitrogenous waste product is:

options.option_text: Urea — formed in the liver via the ornithine/urea cycle; less toxic than ammonia
Ammonia — ammonotelic organisms such as fish excrete ammonia directly in water
Uric acid — uricotelic organisms such as birds and reptiles excrete uric acid as paste
Creatinine — creatinine is a minor waste product, not the PRIMARY nitrogenous product

questions.explanation: NITROGENOUS EXCRETION TYPES: AMMONOTELIC (NH3): fish, aquatic invertebrates — toxic but diluted by water. UREOTELIC (urea): mammals, terrestrial amphibians — less toxic, requires moderate water. URICOTELIC (uric acid): birds, reptiles, insects — nearly insoluble; excreted as paste; saves water. UREA CYCLE (ornithine cycle): liver converts toxic ammonia → urea. BUN: Blood Urea Nitrogen is a clinical kidney function indicator. PYQ: ureotelic/ammonotelic/uricotelic classification in SSC CGL, UPSC biology.

questions.stem: Anti-diuretic hormone (ADH) is released when blood osmolarity increases. Its primary action is to:

options.option_text: Increase water reabsorption in the collecting duct, producing more concentrated urine
Increase urine production to rapidly flush excess solutes from the blood
Stimulate increased sodium secretion into the tubule to balance osmolarity directly
Cause vasoconstriction of the afferent arteriole to reduce glomerular filtration rate

questions.explanation: ADH (Vasopressin): secreted by posterior pituitary. TRIGGER: high blood osmolarity (dehydration) or low blood volume. ACTION: inserts aquaporin channels in collecting duct → more water reabsorbed → concentrated urine. ALCOHOL SUPPRESSES ADH: alcohol inhibits ADH → more dilute urine → dehydration. ALDOSTERONE: increases Na+ reabsorption in DCT → water follows → blood pressure rises. ANP (Atrial Natriuretic Peptide): released at high BP → inhibits ADH + aldosterone → more Na+ and water excreted. PYQ: ADH mechanism in UPSC GS-3, IBPS PO.

questions.stem: Kidney stones (renal calculi) are most commonly composed of:

options.option_text: Calcium oxalate crystals — the most common type of kidney stone worldwide
Sodium chloride deposits — common salt does not precipitate into stones normally
Urea crystals — urea is too soluble to precipitate into stones in normal urine
Iron phosphate compounds — iron is not a common constituent of kidney stones

questions.explanation: KIDNEY STONES: TYPES: (1) Calcium oxalate/phosphate (~75-80%): most common; form when urine is supersaturated with calcium. (2) Uric acid stones (~10%): acidic urine; associated with gout. (3) Struvite stones: magnesium ammonium phosphate; bacterial infections. (4) Cystine stones: rare genetic disorder. LITHOTRIPSY: shock waves break stones without surgery (ESWL). SYMPTOMS: severe flank pain (renal colic), haematuria. PREVENTION: high fluid intake, low-oxalate diet. PYQ: kidney stone composition in SSC CGL, IBPS PO.

questions.stem: Haemodialysis (kidney dialysis) works on the principle of:

options.option_text: Selective diffusion — waste products diffuse out of blood through a semipermeable membrane into dialysate
Reverse osmosis — high pressure forces blood through a membrane; used in water purifiers, not dialysis
Electrophoresis — separates molecules by electrical charge; not the principle of kidney dialysis
Centrifugation — separates by density or weight; not used in artificial kidney machines

questions.explanation: HAEMODIALYSIS: artificial kidney. PRINCIPLE: DIFFUSION across semipermeable membrane (cellulose acetate tubing). Blood pumped through tubing immersed in DIALYSATE (no waste products). WASTE (urea, creatinine, excess salts): diffuse FROM blood (high conc) → dialysate (low conc). USEFUL SUBSTANCES (glucose, normal ions): remain in blood (equal conc in dialysate). PERITONEAL DIALYSIS: uses peritoneum instead of external machine. INDICATION: chronic kidney disease (CKD), acute renal failure. PYQ: dialysis principle in UPSC GS-3, IBPS PO.

questions.stem: The counter-current mechanism in the Loop of Henle is important because it:

options.option_text: Creates a hyperosmotic gradient in the medulla that allows the kidney to produce concentrated urine
Filters blood twice through separate glomeruli to increase waste removal efficiency
Prevents back-flow of urine into the kidney by maintaining directional flow only
Mixes filtrate from different nephrons to average out concentration differences overall

questions.explanation: COUNTER-CURRENT MECHANISM: descending loop (permeable to water, not solutes) → water leaves by osmosis into hypertonic medulla. Ascending loop (impermeable to water, pumps out NaCl) → NaCl pumped into medulla. RESULT: medulla becomes increasingly hypertonic (up to ~1200 mOsm/kg). Collecting duct passing through this gradient (under ADH) → water drawn out → concentrated urine. DESERT MAMMALS: kangaroo rat has very long loops → extremely concentrated urine. VASA RECTA: capillaries maintaining medullary gradient by counter-current exchange. PYQ: counter-current mechanism in UPSC GS-3, discriminating question.
